body:
I appreciate your dedication to compatibility with keeping `height` as the full height so that GDScript code touching this property is unchanged. However, actually, we want to move this over to mid-height. So we would keep it as `sub["height"] = get_height();` here. Above where you have `if (extension != "OMI_collider"`, we would flip around the logic: instead of computing a full height from the mid-height for non-OMI_collider cases, we would compute a mid height from the full height only for OMI_collider cases. And then every place using the height would need to be adjusted, and the docs updated too.

The goal of this class is to represent the data similarly to the glTF file's contents. OMI_collider is deprecated, so we need to focus on the more-modern replacements of OMI_physics_shape, KHR_implicit_shapes, and soon, glTF 2.1's shapes array will replace both of those. All 3 of these define the height of capsules to be the mid-height.

Furthermore, with the OMI_collider stuff as the separate unusual code branch, we can isolate it and wrap it in `#ifndef DISABLE_DEPRECATED`.

As for existing GDScript code expecting full height capsules... it's not really an issue, few users even know the GLTFPhysicsShape class exists, almost nobody is using or manipulating this class in the real world, and potentially actually nobody is specifically manipulating the capsule heights directly from GLTFPhysicsShape. I would just break compatibility and we can move on with the definitions that the glTF ecosystem has chosen. But I would feel better if @lyuma also approved of this approach.

body:
```suggestion
			The effective radius of the shape, in meters. This is used when the shape type is [code]"sphere"[/code]. This property is backed by [member radius_top] and [member radius_bottom], and will return their average when they differ. Setting this property will set the value into both [member radius_top] and [member radius_bottom]. This value should not be negative.
```
